question: The University of Latvia implemented a project entitled ‘Strengthening values-based family literacy and sexuality education in the Latvian education system’1 with funding from the Recovery and Resilience Facility.

Although the grant has closed, the final policy report was presented on 17 March 2026 to the Demography, Family and Children Affairs Subcommittee of the Saeima (Latvian parliament), where its authors called on legislators to incorporate its recommendations into national education standards and guidelines, although no formal decision has yet been taken2.

The recommended materials, based on an abstinence-centred programme also active in other Member States, describe extramarital sexual relations as ‘abuse of the body and person’ and call for fostering ‘a critical attitude towards any sexual activity that is not holistic/complete (including homosexual behaviour)’.
Latvian civil-society organisations and clinical psychologists have questioned the scientific basis for these materials3. 1.

Did the Commission verify this project’s compliance with Article 5(2) of Regulation 2021/241 and Article 21 of the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the European Union when assessing the related milestone, and was it satisfactorily fulfilled?

Will the Commission examine whether EU funding is being used to introduce discriminatory or scientifically unsupported sexuality-education materials into Latvian schools, and, if necessary, require corrective measures, including recovery of funds and conditions for any future related funding?
